Soccer Grannies

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Granny soccer stars from Tzaneen to the world

Summary:
The soccer grannies of Limpopo spear headed by the powerhouse, Mamma Beka, are
making waves around the world. Last year they organised the first ever soccer granny’s
world championship with teams competing from Zambia, the USA, France, Zimbabwe and
Mozambique.

These grannies have such amazing stories of how soccer saved their lives.

Character 1 - Lizzie is 93
her community had labeled her the “crazy granny” and Isolated her, but when Beka reached out to help she realised that Lizzie was suffering from Trauma after losing all 4 of her son’s and having to raise her grandchildren with only a sassa grant.
She was extremely depressed, so Beka forced her to join their soccer
team. Every week she dragged her to the soccer field, and it literally changed her life. I
haven’t seen her play, but Beka says she is one of the best!

Character 2: BULL
She was abused for year, lost all her confidence and faith in humanity basically. But she has fought back and says she is now stronger and fitter than ever. Medically her blood pressure has dropped dramatically.

Character 3. BEKA
Beka speaks so beautifully about what the game means to these women. She herself was
sick and in a wheelchair when she had to start exercising to be able to move again. “I told
myself one day at a time and look at me now. 16 years later and I am a soccer star.”

There are over 1000 grannies playing in teams in Limpopo, Gauteng and KZN, they all
compete against each other in tournaments organized by Beka.
But the grannies have also inspired teams as far as the USA and France



Further information:
Basic story structure

Sunset in Tzaneen and the grannies are playing a match at the stadium
Clearly establishing our 3 main characters in visuals
Intercut with headlines about the grannie soccer world cup and how they have gone global

Early morning Tzaneen
We start in the daily lives of Lizzie and Bull
One is preparing food for her grandchildren, while the other is farming her fields.
Beka is setting up for practice

Practice session - running, foot work, fitness
Lizzie and Bull - How soccer has changed their lives

The world cup
Phone call with team USA
Team USA brag about the original Tzaneen grannies
Visuals of the world cup 2023

Life with Soccer
World cup 2025
End on a match - but this time we see the grannies is a whole new light, because we know them
and we will have Lizzies grandchildren cheering for her this time

22k

beka
She's a strong woman.
she worked hard building herself a house.

VO

i would say I wanna leave. What did I miss? Soccer!

BULL
They say, “Mhan Annah, what are you eating? “ I eat the road I wake up in the morning and run on the street. Every day, every morning I walk up around 6AM and leave I come back around 3 PM
I DON’T HAVE TIME TO PLAY

Lizzie Mongwe is another member of Vakhegula Vakhegula WHO DOESN’T HAVE TIME TO PLAY. She still runs 21km every saturday morning, even at the age of 73


LIZZIE - I don’t worry about being old. I keep running

M - When you are around people don’t SCORE?

BEKA
Mac
how we've seen a change the lives of someone like Lindsey.
I don't think she'll be alive today if she was not playing soccer.

BEKA
Lizzie lost her daughter.
People didn't understand her because of the trauma that she was going through and she felt isolated

I was so happy. I felt so proud of myself. I no longer have problems I am so happy


LIZZIE

BULL
I’ve found family because we don’t shout at each other we don’t fight.


BEKA
we practice, we love, we laugh, we sing, and when we go back home we just sleep and we are free from stress.

a global movement.

I'm the one who started a soccer team there in Togo. They didn't have a soccer team in Zambia.
last year I went there, launched 20 granny soccer team in Zambia
in 2010, we went to America 2014, went to Brazil, 2016, went to Russia. After Russia, 2019 we went to France.

(laughter)
Interviewer : They are say Bonjour
Interviewee : I say “Dumelang Dumelang”

VO
Last year, what began as a dream for Beka become an global success, when she organised the first-ever international soccer grannies World Cup right here in Tzaneen.


BEKA
Remember, FIFA, when they started the World Cup, they had four countries Do you know that?
we had more than 17 teams. Hello? Well, yes, that's absolutely we are the best.

beka

How does it make you feel to see what you have created

And people are cheering for grannies. That's suitable. My gogo.

In 2023 friends, we had one team. Now we have three teams on coming from France, America, we had three teams. I think now we have six that promised us to come. We also have Denmark, Mauritius and many teams that are coming.

back.

BEKA
We do have support, but no money.
We have nothing. But 2025 will succeed.

MacAs South Africans, as ordinary people, what can we learn from the grannies? If we come together, be one. We can do it.
